repo.name: http
repo.description: A composable API for making HTTP requests in Dart.

issue.body:
Just wanted to let you know that this issue is still present on android devices: https://github.com/dart-lang/http/issues/877

I discovered the problem while using the openid_client (https://pub.dev/packages/openid_client).
I configured the authentication process to use an external browsers (See https://github.com/appsup-dart/openid_client/issues/128 for more details) and this is what happens:

- When the authentication process starts the App goes in background and open a browser to desired authentication server URL
- When you log in the browser will be redirected to localhost:4000 with all the relevant data
- However the openUrl on https://github.com/dart-lang/http/blob/ef05b3744424885d93f88a6a50664fb5b7d5cbdb/pkgs/http/lib/src/io_client.dart#L114 fails with the "ClientException with SocketException: Failed host lookup: 'xxx.yyy.zzz' (OS Error: No address associated with hostname, errno = 7)" since the App has been put on background (and the browser is still on foreground)

If you use an inApp webview the problem doesn't occur (since the app is still on foreground)

_(Flutter maintainers pointed me here, original issue: https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/121143)_

When my flutter app goes in to the background it gets SocketExceptions when it tries to make http requests (examples captured by Crashlytics included below). I assume this is something to do with Android OS' energy saver mode, is this expected behavior? Getting failed host lookup exceptions isn't ideal as my app would like to take a different course of action if a hostname can't be reached compared to the app is being restricted by the host os. Ideally this would raise an Exception unique to this situation that I could handle differently (eg: `SocketException: Resource restricted` or similar).

issue.body:
It's quite common in larger business intranets that connections are only secured by self-signed certificates. To enable secure communication inside such networks, we're currently relying on `HttpClient`'s `badCertificateCallback`. 

That works well - but for http2 support and honoring of proxies set on device level, we would like to switch to cronet for Android. However, in our tests, the `badCertificateCallback` is never invoked. Instead attempted requests simply fail with a ClientException:

```
ClientException: Cronet exception: m.mb: Exception in CronetUrlRequest: net::ERR_CERT_AUTHORITY_INVALID, ErrorCode=11, InternalErrorCode=-202, Retryable=false, uri=https://self-signed.badssl.com/
```

Is it possible to support the `badCertificateCallback` with cronet? Or is there an alternative way to accept self-signed certificates?

It means that, whenever you are using an external browser to manage the authentication process and the App (using this package) goes in background and the authentication process fails with error:
ClientException with SocketException: Failed host lookup: 'xxx.yyy.zzz' (OS Error: No address associated with hostname, errno = 7)

The only way, I discovered, to solve the situation is:

  • Using LaunchMode.inAppWebView (please be aware webview don't support self signed certificates!)
urlLauncher(String url) async {
    var uri = Uri.parse(url);
    await launchUrl(uri, 
        mode: LaunchMode.inAppWebView,
      );
  }
  • Configuring the Android manifest to use clear text traffic (see: #16)

It could be usefull to add these informations on the docs

comments.body_html:
@brianquinlan, it works using package:cronet_http on Android Devices!

However please be aware that this HTTP client won't support the classic "badCertificateCallback" to manage self signed certificates without creating a custom CA to install on all the machines you want to use (#1314) ^^

It should be doable by using the native CronetEngine.Builder(..) with a drugged TrustManager that will accept any certificate by your own specific internal logic, but as far as I understood, the current flutter package cronet_http doesn't allow to add this options on the native CronetEngine
